measurement: NeMo file-driven ceiling, cache-aware RNNT, the frozen method

method.note: constants.py freezes this method; nothing in bench executes it, so it is a scripted run

wer.note: identical between the eager and graphed arms at each batch, to every digit printed

reads: At batch 32 the graph path is worth x1.29 on upstream's own file-driven path. Real, and far short of what would close a capacity gap of this size.

At batch 128 it is worth nothing (x0.96, inside the eager arm's own 16% spread). The step stops being host-launch-bound once the batch is large enough, which is the whole mechanism the graph path addresses.
The graphed and eager arms produce the same WER to every printed digit at each batch, which is the expected result: upstream asserts torch.equal against eager, not a tolerance.
The eager batch-128 arm spreads 16% of its own median across five repeats, so a ratio inside about 1.16 at that batch is not distinguishable from noise here.

denominator.note: the largest ceiling the frozen method names; the MVP bar is 0.8 of it
